title: Supporting Local Entrepreneurs in Enhancing Sanitation - SEED Madagascar

facts.fact: The SEED Madagascar blog post 'Supporting Local Entrepreneurs in Enhancing Sanitation' was published on 17 November 2021.
SEED has so far established 103 village savings and loan association (VSLA) groups, as stated in its November 2021 article.
facts.quote: SEED have so far established 103 VSLA groups.

facts.fact: So far, 17 masons have applied their training from SEED, UNICEF and CARA to set up their own sanitary product businesses.
facts.quote: So far 17 masons have applied their training to set up their own sanitary product businesses.

facts.fact: VSLA groups use collective village savings as a source of zero-interest loans so the whole community can buy sanitary products.
facts.quote: the collective savings of which are used as a source of zero-interest loans.

facts.fact: SEED partnered with UNICEF and CARA, the regional business centre for the Anosy region, in June to train masons in entrepreneurship and San Plat design.
facts.quote: In June SEED partnered with UNICEF and CARA, the regional business centre for the Anosy region, to train masons in entrepreneurship and San Plat design.

facts.fact: San Plats are mason-built small concrete slabs for household latrine platforms that improve hygiene and reduce smell thanks to a tight-fitting lid.
facts.quote: mason-built sanitary platforms for household latrines (San Plats). These small concrete slabs can improve hygiene through ease of cleaning, reduce smell thanks to a tight-fitting lid

facts.fact: The article was published on Wednesday, 17 November 2021 and written by Adèle Pavé.
SEED Madagascar is registered as a UK charity with charity number 1079121.
SEED Madagascar's site lists a GlobalGiving Vetted award from 2019.
